subject: Sizing + guaranteed throughput / reserved-commit discount ask (Helix Therapeutics)
messages:
From: Danielle Wu <d.wu@helixtx.com>

Cc: Procurement Ops <procure@helixtx.com>, Helix Technical Lead <infra@helixtx.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jan 2028 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity ask — guaranteed throughput + discount for reserved commit

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency and observability. We are evaluating a dedicated capacity path for our clinical-research assistant (internal tool) and a customer-facing triage API. Before we go to procurement we need two things clarified for our security and finance teams:

1) A firm throughput guarantee for a reserved commit (p95 token latency and tokens/sec throughput) for a steady-state and a peak window.
2) A pricing example and discount band if we commit to 12 months vs 36 months (including any ramp/burst allowances).

To help you size, here's the current expected workload (rough numbers):
- Steady: ~600 req/min (10 rps), median response length ~220 tokens, median context 1,536 tokens.
- Peak: ~2,200 req/min (~36.7 rps) for 30–45 minute windows during clinical shifts, response length up to 600 tokens.
- Concurrent active sessions: up to ~180 concurrent inference streams (mostly short-lived).
- Model mix: 70% open-Llama family (optimized), 30% larger/finetuned checkpoints for sensitive outputs.
- Latency target: p95 token latency under 400ms for customer-facing API; internal can tolerate up to 700ms.

I've attached sample request logs and the draft term sheet from procurement. Can you confirm a recommended GPU pool size and an example pricing tier (including any credits for unused burst)? Procurement needs a straw man by EOD Wednesday.

Appreciate it — Danielle

--
Danielle Wu
Director, Platform Engineering
Helix Therapeutics

Thanks for the clear numbers and the term sheet. Quick read-through: nothing blocking. We'll size conservatively and give you a couple of configuration options (baseline reserved pool + burst bucket) and a 12v36 month discount matrix.

A couple quick clarifying asks that will materially change sizing:
- Are the 600 req/min steady requests uniformly distributed, or do you have minute-level bursts inside that steady period?
- For the 600/min steady, what is the expected average completion tokens (not median) — we ask because batching benefits more from longer completions.
- Any expected growth ramp in the first 90 days? (e.g., +10–30% M/M)

I'll loop in Karthik and Marcus for throughput modeling and Naomi on the pricing lanes. Expect a sizing matrix and two config proposals from us tomorrow morning.

Best,
Aisha

From: karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
To: aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com, Helix Technical Lead <infra@helixtx.com>, Danielle Wu <d.wu@helixtx.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ask — sizing + pricing straw man

Folks — I ran the numbers and sketched a compact sizing matrix. Key assumptions up front:
- Model baseline throughput per GPU (A100-80GB class, quantized Llama variant) for this workload ~= 12k output tokens/sec under continuous batching and our KV cache for 1.5k context. H100-class effective throughput ~= 26k tokens/sec.
- We size for peak sustained 45-minute windows plus a steady-state baseline. We also include a burst pool for rare spikes.

Quick math (peak window):
- Peak rps: 36.7 rps * 420 tokens avg = 15,414 tokens/sec.
- Safety factor: +25% (headroom for model mix and unpredictable tails) => target 19,268 tokens/sec.
- Recommended baseline options:
  Option A (cost-efficient): 2x H100 (equiv throughput ~52k tokens/sec) with explicit concurrency tuning (allowing 40 streams/GPU). This covers peak and leaves room for M/M growth; recommended for teams prioritizing lower latency headroom and simpler autoscale.
  Option B (balanced reserved + burst): 3x A100-80GB reserved (3 * 12k = 36k tokens/sec) + 1x A100 burst pool for short windows (adds 12k tokens/sec). Effective peak capacity = 48k tokens/sec; recommended if you prefer reserved commits on A100 families for pricing predictability.
  Option C (minimum safe reserved): 2x A100-80GB reserved (24k tokens/sec) with automated burst to 4x A100 during peaks and longer tail-based fallback to smaller models. This lowers up-front commit cost but requires reliable burst policies.

Latency notes: with continuous batching and a 50–80ms service overhead we expect p95 token latency under 350–400ms for the H100 option and ~400–550ms for the A100 configs depending on batch windows. If Helix wants p95 <350ms for customer-facing API consistently, go H100s.

Pricing/discount straw man (illustrative):
- 12m commit on Option B (3x A100 reserved): 18% discount off list + 1 week/month burst credits (250 GPU-hours/month) for the first 3 months.
- 36m commit on Option B: 28% discount + 2 weeks/month burst credits and 5% usage credits applied to first invoice.
- Option A (H100) carries a premium (~25% higher list price) but tighter latency SLOs; discounts scale similarly for 12/36m.

Next steps:
- If Helix confirms preferred option (A/B/C) we'll generate a formal term sheet with the exact monthly GPU-hour commitments, SLA clauses (p95 lat, uptime), and an explicit burst-credit accounting example.
- Naomi: can you turn the illustrative discount matrix into numbers for the term sheet (list price -> discounted monthly fees + effective $/token estimate)?

Cc'ing Marcus for any throughput caveats (model mix, quantization impact).

-Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Danielle / team —

Thanks for the fast turnaround. Per internal review, our recommended go-forward for procurement (best balance of latency, cost, and predictability):

- Proposal: Option B (3x A100-80GB reserved) + 1x A100 burst pool (automated up to 4x A100 for 60-minute windows).
- 12-month commit: 20% off list for the reserved pool; includes 200 GPU-hours/month of burst credit for the first quarter.
- 36-month commit: 30% off list; includes 400 GPU-hours/month of burst credit for first 6 months + one-time migration assistance credit (engineering hours).
- SLA: p95 token latency target for customer-facing API <= 420ms on reserved + burst config; we will include a performance clause that allows Helix to request a model-tuning pass if regressions occur.

Attached: term_sheet_draft_v2.pdf (pricing table filled) and sizing_matrix.xlsx (detailed calculations). If this looks good, Aisha will hand to procurement and we can get a redline-ready contract by next week.

Best,
Naomi
